# [TASK] Replace regex voice-command matcher with Ollama-based multilingual intent parsing

## Task
Replace `voiceCommands.js`'s regex matcher with Ollama-based multilingual
intent classification.

## Scope
Command-parsing layer only — does not change transcription (#212) or
language selection (#213).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A transcript in either English or German maps to the correct canonical command (genre/category, search, theme toggle, logout) via an LLM prompt, not per-language regex tables
- [x] Phrasing variance within a language ("light mode" vs. "switch to light mode" vs. "make it light") resolves to the same command
- [x] No confident match returns a clear "no matching command" result, same contract `parseVoiceCommand` has today
- [x] `VoiceControl.test.jsx`/`voiceCommands` tests updated for both languages and phrasing variance, not just the old fixed English phrases

## Estimate
**Hours:** 6

## Notes
Uses the same structured-extraction approach as #202, rather than a second way of turning a transcript into an intent.

New `POST /api/v1/ai/voice-command` classifies a transcript (English or German) into LOGOUT / CHANGE_MODE / CHOOSE_GENRE / SEARCH. An incomplete extraction degrades to "no match" instead of dispatching a half-command; a failed model call falls back to searching the raw transcript. `voiceCommands.js` is now a thin client for that endpoint instead of a local regex table.

Known limit: the tests mock the model, so they prove the contract, not real bilingual accuracy. Live accuracy is #215's job.
